notes: Most complete coverage, including the quoted "{}" fallthrough as in the reference, with thorough tests; repeating inline Quoted() checks instead of a helper makes the code noisier.

The most complete fix: it covers every brace check, including the quoted "{}" branch in directive(), and misses only the HasSuffix address check. It repeats inline `!Token().Quoted()` checks instead of using a helper, but its tests across dispenser, parser, formatter and an adapt case are thorough.

Covers every dispenser and parser brace check with Dispenser-level helpers, but uses inline Token checks in doImport, which is slightly inconsistent; it also leaves the quoted "{}" fallthrough and the address HasSuffix check unchanged.

Dispenser-level helpers correctly cover the parser and dispenser paths, though doImport mixes in an inline token check. It misses the "{}" and HasSuffix cases, but its tests are strong, including a heredoc case, formatter checks and a richer adapt test.
Clean Token helpers fix the reported issue, but the anonymous-block check on the import block-mapping key still compares only the value, and the quoted "{}" case is not addressed.

Good Token-helper approach that fixes the core issue. It leaves the doImport anonymous-block check (`currentMappingKey == "{"`) unfixed, plus the "{}" and HasSuffix cases, and its tests are adequate but narrower with no adapt test.

Nearly identical to the reference, using Token helper methods applied consistently across dispenser and parser; it only skips the minor quoted "{}" and address-suffix refinements, and adds solid dispenser, parse, snippet and adapt tests.

Clean Token helpers mirror the reference across the dispenser and parser and fix the reported case. It misses the quoted "{}" branch in directive() and the HasSuffix address check, and its tests (dispenser, parse table, snippet, adapt) are solid.

Compact recursive slugBase with cmp.Or fallback; the `dir != Base()` guard never matches because of the leading-slash mismatch, so Dir is effectively always set (harmless but shows a misunderstanding); the test covers resources, taxonomy and term but not nested section slugs.

A clean recursive slugBase closely mirrors the reference, Dir is only set when it differs from the default, and cmp.Or keeps CreateTargetPaths minimal; the test covers section, bundle resource, taxonomy and term slugs but not nested slugged sections.

Clean recursive slugBaseDir/pathBase closely mirrors the reference, keeps all logic in hugolib, and sets Dir only when a slug is present; the integration test covers nested section, taxonomy and term slugs.

It is close to the reference: a recursive slugBaseDir plus a pathBase helper, with Dir set only when a slug is present, giving minimal impact on unaffected pages; the solid integration test covers nested slugs, term listing links and unaffected English paths, though it sits in a generic test file.

Works, but it always computes and uses SluggedDir, which makes the `!= ""` checks dead code, and it relies on an unchecked `CurrentSection().(*pageState)` assertion spread across three helpers; the test is the most thorough (bundles, url override, partial-language sections, terms).

Correctly applies ancestor section, taxonomy and term slugs to both branch and leaf paths, but SluggedDir is always populated and root pages get "/" instead of "", which widens the blast radius, and it relies on unchecked *pageState type assertions; its test is the most thorough (resources, url override, nested slugs, non-section subdirs, default-language term slug).

Applies slugs along the ancestor section chain and only overrides paths when a slug exists, which keeps risk low; the leaf-path prefix rewrite inside CreateTargetPaths is a bit scattered, but the test covers nested sections, taxonomy and term.

It works by building an ancestor slice per page and returning the slugged section base only when a slug exists, but the leaf-path logic is split into string-prefix replacement inside CreateTargetPaths, which is less cohesive; the test covers nested slugged sections and taxonomy/term.

Matches the reference approach (slice plus a knownImports.Has check at instance expansion) and has thorough regression tests, but it adds a redundant static dedup in FindImportStatements that ignores module instance keys and can wrongly drop a child block for other module instances.

Fixes the reported bug and adds the reference's per-instance first-wins check in expandResourceImports, but its extra static pre-dedup compares only the resource instance key: root blocks for `module.m["x"].res` and `module.m["y"].res` collide and the second is still silently dropped.

Fixes the reported same-module case by storing a slice per ConfigResource, but any ancestor import for a resource still drops every child-module block for it, so per-instance parent override is wrong and 2 of 3 hidden tests fail.
Simple fix that keeps every same-module block, but any ancestor import for the ConfigResource still discards all of the child module's blocks, and its unit test locks in that coarse behavior.

Returns a slice and keeps child blocks unless an ancestor targets the same static key, but a dynamic for_each child block is dropped outright when the parent overrides one instance, and the patch adds a configs method and child sorting that the fix did not need.

Per-instance ancestor override works only for static resource keys: dynamic blocks still lose to the ancestor wholesale, module instance keys are ignored, and it adds an unneeded configs.Import method and child-sorting change.

Handles static per-instance parent override by comparing absolute addresses, but it drops whole dynamic child blocks and has no first-wins check at expansion, so precedence can flip in module-instance cases; it fails one hidden test.

Keeps all same-module blocks and compares full static instance addresses across modules, but if either side is dynamic it drops the child's whole block, and it has no expansion-time dedup, so an overlapping child block can overwrite the parent's.

Works for the main cases and adds solid unit and integration tests, but calls DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts unnecessarily (so --once can fail on invalid script shortcut combos it should override), detects the flag via Value.String()=="true", and adds unrelated proxy-clearing TestMain changes.

The --once logic works, but it detects the flag with a hacky string comparison and calls DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts unnecessarily, which can error on configs that --once should simply override. It also adds unrelated TestMain proxy-env clearing in two test packages.

Focused post-consolidation rewrite that preserves exec/env/tags/options and clears shortcuts, with a thorough table test plus integration tests that check single execution and the multi-scenario error; it shares the gaps of no lower-layer shortcut dropping and no execution-segment conflict check.

Applies the rewrite after consolidation like the reference and preserves exec, env, tags and options with cloned maps. It rejects multiple scenarios and the conflicting CLI shortcuts, and is backed by good unit and end-to-end tests. It misses two things: env/config-file shortcuts silently wiping script scenarios before --once runs, and the execution-segment conflicts.

Rewrites the scenario correctly at the end of consolidation and keeps exec, env, tags and options; it misses three things the reference handles: a lower-layer shortcut (e.g. K6_DURATION env) wiping the script's scenarios before the rewrite, --execution-segment conflicts, and override warnings; it also widens the getConsolidatedConfig signature.

The transformation is correct but runs inside getConsolidatedConfig by threading the pflag.FlagSet through its signature, which couples consolidation to CLI flags. Its consolidation and unit tests are solid. Like the others, it ignores lower-layer shortcuts and execution segments.

Clean standalone once.go applied after consolidation with exit codes and cloned maps; it always sets exec explicitly (turning unset into "default"), does not drop lower-layer shortcuts or reject execution-segment flags, and has good unit and consolidation tests but no end-to-end run test.

A clean separate once.go applied after consolidation in test_load, with a non-mutation guarantee and reasonable tests. It always writes exec explicitly, so an unset exec becomes "default". It shares the same gaps with lower-layer shortcuts and execution segments.

Mirrors the reference (unary-plus wrapper plus the Pretty fix) and additionally preserves the parse-time positive, division and modulo checks through the wrapper; the tests are good but include 'FIXME: this position looks wrong' comments that lock in odd pre-existing error positions.

Uses the same unary-plus wrapper as the reference, fixes Pretty, and keeps the parse-time positive, division-by-zero and modulo-by-zero checks by looking through the wrapper; its tests are thorough, but it leaves FIXME comments in the test table and the wrapper's position starts at the literal rather than the opening paren.

Clean, focused unary-plus wrapping that also looks through the wrapper for the positive, div-by-zero and mod-by-zero parse checks, with solid AST and printer tests, but it leaves DurationExpr.Pretty printing the wrapper as '(+5)', inconsistent with String().

Clean unary-plus wrapping that keeps the positive, div and mod parse-time checks via an unwrap helper with good parser and printer tests, but it does not update DurationExpr.Pretty, so the prettier would render the new node as '(+5)'.

Fixes round-trip and keeps positive-duration validation, but introduces a new sentinel Op=0 AST shape that forces edits to durations.go, printer, prettier, ast and translate_ast (emitting an empty op to API/UI consumers), which is more invasive and fragile than reusing unary ADD.

Fixes the round-trip but adds a new AST shape with Op=0 (the ERROR item type) as a sentinel, which forces changes in the printer, prettier, ast PositionRange, the duration evaluator and the web API translator (now emitting an empty op); this is invasive and fragile for other AST consumers, and div/mod-by-(0) checks are no longer caught at parse time.

Wraps a bare literal in a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr like the reference, and keeps the parse-time positive-duration check for (0) and -(5) via a recursive constant evaluator; it also updates Pretty and adds evaluation tests, but changes ast.go PositionRange, uses an awkward pointer-as-optional parameter, and drops the parse-time div/mod-by-(0) check.

Uses the reference's unary-plus approach with paren-inclusive positions (via a small ast.go PositionRange tweak) and fixes Pretty; it keeps the positive-duration and out-of-range checks through a recursive constant evaluator and adds parser, printer, prettier and eval tests, though div/mod by (0) moves to runtime as in the reference.

Propagating the error through the template store works for partials and pipelines. However, it intrusively modifies the forked parse package and templatestore, keeps a now-meaningless bool return in applyTransformations, edits exec.go without the fork script, and loses values returned across template boundaries.

Return wrapping is done by editing the forked Go parser (parse.go), the kind of fork intrusion the issue warns against; it also leaves a vestigial bool return, turns bare returns into errors that only TemplateStore paths swallow, loses values returned inside nested templates, and fails one hidden test.

Uses a sentinel error/panic with the return value carried in context, so a valued return inside a `template`/`define` still reaches the enclosing partial. It passes everything, but the context value leaks into nested non-partial executions such as render hooks, `return x | f` silently drops the pipeline tail, and exec.go is edited without updating the fork script.

A ctx-scoped PartialReturn holder plus a returnSignal panic gives early return everywhere and keeps values set inside nested template calls in partials (passes all hidden tests); weaknesses are direct edits to the forked exec.go without updating the fork script, a .Render inside a partial being able to set the partial's value, and silently dropping trailing pipeline commands, which the rewritten 13600 test now treats as correct.

A sound state-held return holder with nested isolation, and it updates the fork script. It still discards returned values at template boundaries, does not handle `return x | f` (tail silently dropped), moves `return` into the templates namespace without need, and leaves the docs half-updated.

The ctx-holder sentinel design works, and the walkTemplate change is also added to the fork script so it survives re-forking; however, walkTemplateRoot drops returned values inside nested template calls, `return x | f` silently skips `f`, and it fails one hidden test.

Clean ReturnError sentinel with a context capture that is cleared for nested executions, and it rewrites both `return a b` and `return x | f` correctly. However, walkReturnable discards valued returns at template boundaries, so a value returned from a define/template inside a partial is lost (likely the failing hidden test). It also makes unrequested doc edits.

The ctx-captured ReturnError design is clean, pipe/multi-arg returns are wrapped sensibly, a template rendered via .Render inside a partial is kept from overriding the partial's return value, and tests are thorough; drawbacks are direct edits to the forked exec.go (errRecover and walkTemplate) without a script update, swallowing returned values inside nested template calls, and failing one hidden test.
